summary: # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial: Dress Making - Making Lantern Sleeves ## Editing the Sleeve Next, we need to edit the sleeve. 1. In the virtual model arm position, click on the center point. 2. At this blue point, create a straight line point. 3. After selecting the extension tool, click on the center point at the top, then click on the center point at the bottom to create a baseline. 4. Rotate a side of the plate to make the bottom have more volume. 5. After creating, click on the center point at the bottom. 6. Adjust the shape of the plate. ## Stretching the Sleeve In the process of stretching the bottom: 1. Click on the control key to change it along the original rhythm. 2. Select the line at the bottom of the sleeve plate and also click on the control key to stretch along the original rhythm. 3. Select the line at the top of the sleeve plate, and click on the control key to change it along the original rhythm. ## Simulating the Sleeve The sleeve has been a little bit twisted here. This occurs because we just fixed it to the virtual model with a sewing needle, which means the width of the sleeve is not enough. 1. After stretching, simulate the clothes. 2. After simulation, you can see that the sleeves are much smoother. ## Adjustments to the Sleeve Then, make some adjustments: 1. Adjust the length of the sleeve. 2. Widen the sleeve a little bit. 3. After the modification, turn the bottom straight line point into a curve line point to make the curve line smoother. 4. Use the edge curve point tool to adjust the curve line at the bottom. ## Fine-Tuning the Simulation After simulation, reduce the particle diameter to 10 to achieve a better simulation effect. ## Creating the Opening Plate After creating the sleeve plate, create the opening plate to make the embroidery effect: 1. Use the rectangle tool to drag in the 2D window to create an opening plate. 2. Use the edge curve tool to select the width of the plate; usually, 15 to 20 centimeters is more suitable. 3. Use the line sewing tool to sew these plates together. ## Arranging the Wrist Area After sewing, arrange the arrangement points near the wrist: 1. Use the positioning ball to move it to a position that can cover the virtual model wrist. 2. After this simulation, if you find you won't be able to pass your arm, widen the sleeve bottom according to your needs. ## Making the Belt After that, you have to make a belt: 1. The waist plate can be shortened a little bit. Use the edge curve measurement tool to click on the waist. 2. Since the clothing measurement board has passed the belt and the sleeve, you need to adjust its diameter. 3. After adjustment, use the edge curve measurement tool to select the measurement board to adjust its position. 4. After modifying the diameter, move the measurement board to apply the change. ## Removing Extra Plates Now, we have finished the measurement board removal. You can remove the extra plates with the same operation as before. 1. If the rated pins may disappear during the process, please add them back. 2. Eliminate excess plates and remove any that are not needed. ## Finalizing the Belt Plate After cutting some of the plates, if the felt is not close enough, pull out some ropes to tighten the lower board. 1. Next, let's make a belt plate. First, select the bottom 100 part of the front and back pieces. 2. In the attribute editor, check their 2D line length. 3. Use the rectangle tool to click on the 2D window; the width is the measurement value, and the height is set according to your needs. 4. After creation, check the 3D window plate effect and adjust it accordingly. ## Adjusting the Belt 1. Adjust the width according to your preference. 2. After arranging the plate, select the line cutting tool. 3. Click on the belt first, then press the Shift key. Click on the top line each time, then release the Shift key. 4. Merge the sides together. 5. After merging, change to the leather surface; this will make the surface flatter. 6. Finally, we will see the result. Now, let's change the width of the belt once more by clicking on the belt.
